idiom.source: the uct and fork-join-create adapters + so_5::introduce_child_coop (environment.hpp) + environment_t::deregister_coop
idiom.note: a split registers one child coop holding the four children on their direct mboxes; the parent deregisters it once all four have confirmed; thread_pool(cores) with fifo_t::individual for cores>=2

caveats: cores>=2 uses the thread_pool dispatcher with exactly `cores` work threads and fifo_t::individual (one demand queue per agent, agents of one coop free to run on different threads); cores=1 uses one_thread. The work threads are pinned one per CPU from the harness's set through a custom so_5::disp::abstract_work_thread_factory_t

the pool places agents dynamically: which thread runs a given agent's next demand is the dispatcher's decision, so how many hand-offs cross a core is not fixed and not reported, where qb's cell fixes actor a on core a % cores
wait=1 maps to mpmc combined_lock_factory with a 10 s spin budget (never reached inside a hop); wait=0 maps to simple_lock_factory (mutex + condition variable)
max_demands_at_once is SObjectizer's shipped default, 4 -- the batching knob CAF spells max-throughput=300 and qb spells draining the pipe; it was not tuned
Messages derive from so_5::message_t and travel on each agent's DIRECT mbox, the framework's own fast path

SObjectizer creates agents only inside a cooperation registered with the environment: every split here registers one child coop of four agents and its parent deregisters it after their ConfirmExits -- 341 coops per repetition at the defaults

quadrants bind to the same thread_pool as their parent and the pool places them, so with cores=2 the quadtree is spread over the work threads dynamically; qb's cell keeps each of the root's subtrees on one core because qb has no cross-core spawn -- see benchmarks/savina/facloc.md
